long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Gomel in 1972, Andrey Melnichenko studied physics in Moscow before leaving university amid the Soviet collapse. He began with currency-exchange booths, founded MDM Bank in 1993 and later redirected banking proceeds into industrial assets. Working with Sergei Popov, he assembled fertilizer producer EuroChem and thermal-coal supplier SUEK; Forbes now describes fertilizers and coal as the source of his self-made fortune.

Melnichenko withdrew as beneficiary of the trust holding those companies and resigned their boards in 2022. EuroChem says he no longer controls the company, while Bloomberg continues to attribute the stakes to him for wealth-ranking purposes because he founded them and identifies EuroChem as his largest asset. His yachting history follows a similarly ambitious design thread: he commissioned two Philippe Starck projects named A, culminating in the 143-metre Sailing Yacht A.
